info.title: Hyper CDC Orchestrator API
info.description:
Unified CDC control-plane API for Debezium engine lifecycle, Kafka Connect,
governed pipelines (replica, stream, and lakehouse landing), logs, notifications,
and metrics. Canonical prefix: `/cdc/*`.
See docs/architecture/hyper-cdc-orchestrator-design.html (Ch.12) for the datalake contract.

post.summary: Enable/disable profile (enable reconciles Connect)
start | pause | resume | restart | stop | resync (reconciles Kafka Connect)
post.description:
**Test initial sync** — `start` (or `restart`) with `row_limit` is a connectivity and
configuration check, not a production sync. It starts the pipeline, copies up to
`row_limit` rows per table into the target, then stops it: source offsets are reset and
both connectors are deleted. The profile ends `stopped` with a
`profile_test_initial_sync` history entry listing per-table row counts. If any step
fails, the connectors are still removed and the profile ends `failed`. Trigger and
incremental `source_to_target` pipelines only.

`resync` with `row_limit` copies a capped sample and keeps the pipeline running.

`clear_target` is rejected (400) on pipelines with any `rolling_window` table: the
window only re-reads recent rows, so older rows would stay missing. Use
`POST /cdc/profiles/{id}/initial-load` to rebuild the target instead. This also
applies to the scheduled full refresh.

parameters.name: row_limit
parameters.description: With start/restart, runs a test initial sync and stops afterwards. With resync, caps the copied sample.

parameters.name: clear_target
parameters.description: Truncate the mapped target tables before copying (test initial sync / resync).

post.summary: Move some tables into a new Draft pipeline with the same source and target
post.description:
Creates a copy of the pipeline restricted to the selected tables (their mappings and
per-table poll rules move with them), saved as a **Draft** — never started. The new
pipeline gets its own connector/sink names, Kafka topic prefix and replication slot
(a slot pinned in `source.connection.slot` is dropped from the copy). The selected
tables are removed from the original's saved configuration; if the original is
running/paused its connectors keep them until it is restarted
(`original_restart_required`) — start the new pipeline first, then restart the
original. Rejected for trigger capture, OLake, pipelines without an explicit table
list, moving every table, or a name whose connector / topic prefix is already used.
Audit: `profile.split` on both pipelines.

original.description: Original pipeline after the split (secrets redacted)

post.summary: Copy a pipeline as a new Draft under a new name (original untouched)
post.description:
Full copy of the pipeline — source and target connections (secrets included), capture
mode, schedule, every table, mapping and per-table poll rule — saved as a **Draft**,
never started. The copy gets its own id, connector/sink names and Kafka topic prefix
derived from the new name; a slot pinned in `source.connection.slot` is dropped. Unlike
`split`, the original is not modified and any capture mode or pattern is allowed: use
the copy as a template and edit tables, target and keys before starting it. Rejected
for an empty name or a name whose connector / topic prefix is already used.
Audit: `profile.duplicate` on both pipelines.

400.description: Empty name, or name collides with an existing pipeline / connector / topic prefix

post.summary: Start a background initial load (streaming copy of every source row)
post.description:
Copies every row of the selected source tables into the PostgreSQL target, in the
background. Each table is read with **one** forward-only `SELECT *` through
cdc-jdbc-admin (`/v1/stream`) and inserted in batches with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`,
so it can run beside a live pipeline (fresher upserts win) and can be re-run after a
failure. Use it for rows a rolling window never re-reads (e.g. legacy rows with a NULL
UPDATE_DATE). One load per pipeline at a time; job state lives in memory on the
orchestrator instance, and the outcome is written to the profile history
(`profile_initial_load*`) and audit log (`profile.initial_load`).

400.description: Not a source_to_target pipeline, non-PostgreSQL target, jdbc-admin not configured, unknown table, or a load is already running

get.summary: Progress of the latest initial load

200.description: Load status with per-table row counts

404.description: No initial load has run for this pipeline on this instance

delete.description: Stops between insert batches. Rows already copied are kept.

200.description: Current status (state becomes cancelled once the copy stops)

404.description: No initial load has run for this pipeline on this instance

post.summary: Validate a tool profile without saving (pgcopy, redisshake, mongocopy, pgdump, rsync)
Test a connection from the tool's sidecar
post.description:
Connects from the sidecar container (where the tool runs), so it proves the same network
path and login a run will use. pgcopy: PostgreSQL (warns when the image's pg_dump is older
than the server); pgloader: PostgreSQL target, MySQL/SQL Server source (pgloader --dry-run),
SQLite/CSV files inside the container; mongocopy: mongosh ping/version; redisshake: AUTH,
PING and INFO (warns when the Cluster switch does not match). A failed connection is a
normal answer `{ok: false, target, error, hint}`; success is `{ok: true, target, facts[],
warning?}`. `********` is replaced by the saved password from `profile_id` (`side`) only
when engine, host, port and username are unchanged; otherwise 400.

connection.description: type, host, port, database (or file path), username, password

options.description: TLS/cluster switches, auth database, CSV separator, sslmode

post.summary: Save a tool profile
Start a job from a saved profile
post.description:
Every run is a new job with its own id; the job carries `profile_id`, and the profile's
`last_job_id` points at it. Sidecars keep the newest runs per profile (default 10; Redis 15).
A profile can have one active run: starting another returns 400 with the sidecar's
"already running" message.

post.summary: Stop a running job

get.description:
Status is starting | running | succeeded | completed_with_errors | failed | stopped.
Carries artifact {name, format, bytes, sha256, local_deleted}, tables_dumped / tables_restored,
uploads[] (one per SFTP destination: status pending|uploading|uploaded|failed|stopped,
bytes_sent, remote_path, host_key_fingerprint, host_key_verified, error, hint), and on failure
error, first_error and an operator hint. download_path is set while the local file exists.
A failed upload makes the job completed_with_errors and keeps the local file.

delete.summary: Delete a finished pgdump job and its dump file

get.description:
Streams the dump file from the cdc-pgdump sidecar. Headers Content-Disposition and
X-Dump-Sha256. 400 while the job is running (sidecar 409) or when no file exists (sidecar 410),
including after the local copy was removed because every SFTP destination has it.

post.summary: Test a Postgres connection from the pgdump sidecar and describe the database
post.description:
Connects from the cdc-pgdump container (where pg_dump runs), so it proves the same network
path and credentials a dump will use. A failed connection is a normal answer:
`{ok: false, target, error, hint}`. On success: `{ok: true, target, latency_ms, server_version,
server_major, client_version, client_major, compatible, current_user, database_bytes, ssl,
schemas: [{name, tables, bytes}]}`; `compatible` is false (with a hint) when the server is
newer than pg_dump. A password of `********` is replaced by the saved one from `profile_id`
(`side` source|target) only when host, port and username are unchanged; otherwise 400.

connection.description: type, host, port, database, username, password

post.summary: Log in to an SSH host from the rsync sidecar and describe it
post.description:
Logs in from the cdc-rsync container (where relay runs and where direct runs start) and
probes the host: `{ok, target, side, os, arch, rsync_path, rsync_version, gnu_rsync,
path_kind (dir|file|missing), free_bytes, writable, ssh_client, latency_ms,
host_key_fingerprint, host_key_verified, warning?}`. rsync is auto-detected, Homebrew
first (macOS ships openrsync, which lacks progress, ACLs and xattrs). A failed login is a
normal answer: `{ok: false, error, hint}`. Secrets sent as `********` are taken from
`profile_id` only when host, port and username are unchanged; otherwise 400.

endpoint.description: host, port, username, auth (key|password), password, private_key, passphrase, path, host_key_fingerprint, rsync_path

post.summary: Check whether a sync would run direct (source → target) or fall back to relay
post.description:
Logs in to the source with the target key in a forwarded ssh-agent and, from the source,
logs in to the target (`reach_host`/`reach_port` when set). Answers `{direct: true,
transport: direct, target: {os, rsync_path, …}, target_host_key_fingerprint}` or
`{direct: false, transport: relay, error, hint}`. A password target is never direct.

post.summary: Run (or preview) an rsync profile
post.description:
Starts a sidecar job. With `dry_run=true` the run is a preview (`--dry-run
--itemize-changes`): nothing is written on the target and the job carries
`changes: {counts: {create, update, delete, attrs}, items: [{op, kind, path}] (first 500),
truncated}`. In relay mode a preview still refreshes the relay copy (pull), then dry-runs the push.

get.description:
Status is starting | running | succeeded | completed_with_errors | failed | stopped.
`phase` connect|route|sync|pull|push; `transport` direct|relay with `transport_reason`
(why auto fell back); `progress {bytes, percent, rate, eta, files_transferred,
files_to_check, files_total}` while running; `stats` (rsync --stats, snake_case keys, of the
sync or push) and `stats_pull` (relay); `hosts.{source,target}` facts; `host_keys` with
fingerprints and whether they were pinned; `changes` for previews; on failure `error`,
`first_error` and an operator `hint`. rsync exits 23/24/25 (partial, vanished, max_delete)
are completed_with_errors.

delete.summary: Delete a finished rsync job record

get.summary: Relay staging copies on the rsync sidecar
get.description: One per profile (`id` = profile id), kept so relay runs stay incremental. Answer: `{staging: [{id, bytes, modified_at}], free_mb}`.

delete.summary: Free a profile's relay staging copy
delete.description: The next relay run of that profile pulls everything again. 400 while the profile is running. Deleting a profile also removes its staging copy.

row_count.description: Total rows in the table when the live catalog can count them.

primary_key.description: Primary key columns in ordinal order. Empty when the table has no primary key.

capture_mode.description: logical = ongoing WAL CDC; trigger = table triggers when WAL is unavailable; sync_once = copy current rows once then stop; incremental = JDBC poll on a timestamp/id watermark (no WAL, no triggers; hard deletes are not captured)

changelog_retention_hours.description: Trigger capture only. Prune source changelog rows older than this many hours. Omit or 0 disables pruning. Choose a window larger than expected replication lag so unconsumed rows are not dropped.

timestamp_column.description: Incremental capture. Timestamp/watermark column such as updated_at. Combined with incrementing_column this uses JDBC timestamp+incrementing mode.

incrementing_column.description: Incremental capture. Strictly incrementing column, usually the primary key (e.g. id). Required for replica upsert. Append-only tables can use this without a timestamp column.

upsert_key_columns.description: Incremental replica upsert key on the target (text/composite allowed), e.g. [BRANCH_NO, PRO_CODE].

table_poll.description:
Incremental capture: per-table poll strategy overrides. Tables without a rule poll
on timestamp_column / incrementing_column (watermark). Each rolling_window /
full_copy table runs its own query-mode, mode=bulk JDBC source connector
(`{connector}-poll-{schema-table}`; the first one takes the pipeline connector
name when no table uses a watermark) and publishes to the same topic as table mode.

strategy.description:
watermark = JDBC offset on the watermark columns (default).
rolling_window = every poll re-reads rows whose window_column is today or within
the previous window_days days; no offset is kept, so date-only or non-unique
timestamps cannot skip same-day changes. Rows older than the window reach the
target only through an initial load.
full_copy = every poll re-reads the whole table (small tables only).

window_column.description: rolling_window only: date/timestamp column, e.g. UPDATE_DATE.

window_days.description: rolling_window only: previous days included besides today (1 = today + yesterday).

clear_target.description: Truncate each target table just before copying into it.

tables.description: Subset of source.tables (SCHEMA.TABLE) to load. Empty = every selected table.

zone.description: CDC lands bronze or silver. Gold is derived, not captured.

connection.description: S3-compatible endpoint, bucket, keys, and catalog_uri

data_type.description: Shared SQL type; source and target column types must match

identical.description: When true, source and target table/column names match and no remap is applied

tags.description: Free-form labels for grouping and filtering pipelines (e.g. crm, master-data). Trimmed and de-duplicated case-insensitively on save. Omit on update to keep the saved tags; send [] to clear them. Duplicate copies the original's tags. Returned on every profile as `tags`.

pattern.description: source_to_target is database replica (current product). source_to_stream is Event-first (Kafka topics). source_to_lake is Event-first plus Iceberg from Kafka. source_to_olake is Analytics-first (OLake; draft only until Phase 3).

sink_error_policy.description: Source-to-target sink record handling. fail_fast stops logical and incremental sinks on rejected records. dlq continues and writes rejected records with error-context headers. Trigger sinks retain their existing DLQ behavior for backward compatibility.

kind.description: poll = interval-driven JDBC poll (incremental / trigger); stream = continuous log capture; once = one-time snapshot; idle = not running, nothing scheduled.

interval_ms.description: Poll interval the connector runs on. Present for poll pipelines even while idle.

next_tick_at.description: last_tick_at + interval_ms. Aligned to the connector interval, not its exact poll instant.

next_full_refresh_at.description: Equal to the response timestamp when a running pipeline has never refreshed (next sweep runs it).

source_offsets.description: Last source offsets the poll audit read from Kafka Connect.

tables.description: Qualified schema.table names. Defaults to source.tables.

columns.description: Key columns in index order (INCLUDE columns excluded). Expression indexes may carry expression text or be empty.

expression.description: Index has expression keys (omitted when false)

statements.description: Creation DDL only (CREATE SCHEMA/TABLE/INDEX, optionally behind a SQL Server IF guard or inside an Oracle BEGIN EXECUTE IMMEDIATE … END; block). DROP/ALTER/TRUNCATE/DML are rejected.

profile_id.description: Merge the saved profile's target credentials (masked password in the wizard)

unique.description: Column is the primary key or the only column of a unique index

size.description: Character length or numeric precision (jdbc-admin COLUMN_SIZE)

auto_increment.description: Identity / serial / AUTO_INCREMENT column (omitted when false)

indexes.description: Indexes and unique constraints, the primary-key index included. Absent when the inspector does not report them (older cdc-jdbc-admin).

statement.example: CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS analytics
